method: The swing amount p is read as a percentage of the pair span from 50 to 75 (decimal comma accepted), and the tempo as 20 to 400 BPM (decimal accepted). One beat lasts 60000 / BPM milliseconds; an eighth-note pair spans one beat and a sixteenth-note pair spans half a beat. The first note therefore lasts p% of the pair and the second lasts 100 - p%, the long-to-short ratio is p / (100 - p), and the off-beat shift is the second onset minus the straight midpoint, so 50% is 0 ms and 60% pushes the off-beat late by a tenth of the pair. Feel bands follow the standard swing classification: 1:1 straight at 50%, between 1:1 and 2:1 soft swing, 2:1 triplet swing at 66.67% within 0.05 percentage points (so the rounded 66.7 also reads as triplet), between 2:1 and 3:1 hard swing, and 3:1 dotted hard swing at 75%. The grid lists the first four pairs with onsets in milliseconds and in beats. Values are exact notation timing, not a model of human micro-timing, and everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Swing time: swung pairs are classified as straight 1:1, soft swing between 1:1 and 2:1, triplet swing 2:1, hard swing between 2:1 and 3:1, and dotted hard swing 3:1.
Ableton Live reference manual, Using Grooves: groove timing is applied relative to a chosen note base, so an eighth- or sixteenth-note grid sets which pairs are made uneven.
